title: Which notifications arrive?
description:
Simulate the calls a DLL's `DllMain` receives. Write

```cpp
std::vector<std::string> dllMainCalls(const std::vector<std::string>& events, bool disableThreadCalls);
```

`events` describes what happens in the process, in order:

| Event | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"thread start"` | a thread starts |
| `"thread end"` | a thread ends cleanly |
| `"load"` | the program calls `LoadLibraryW` on the DLL |
| `"free"` | the program calls `FreeLibrary` on the DLL |
| `"exit"` | the process exits |

Return the `DllMain` calls in order, as strings: `"PROCESS_ATTACH"`, `"THREAD_ATTACH"`, `"THREAD_DETACH"`, `"PROCESS_DETACH"` and, for process exit, `"PROCESS_DETACH (exit)"`.

The rules:

- The DLL starts unloaded. `load` counts references (lesson 2.03): only the first load sends `PROCESS_ATTACH`, and only the free that brings the count to zero sends `PROCESS_DETACH`. A `free` while unloaded does nothing.
- Thread events only reach `DllMain` while the DLL is loaded, and only if thread calls are not disabled.
- `disableThreadCalls` means `DisableThreadLibraryCalls` is called in `PROCESS_ATTACH`: no `THREAD_` notifications at all.
- `exit` while loaded sends `PROCESS_DETACH (exit)` and nothing after it is processed. `exit` while unloaded sends nothing, and also ends the list.

```
dllMainCalls({ "thread start", "load", "thread start", "thread end", "free" }, false)
    == { "PROCESS_ATTACH", "THREAD_ATTACH", "THREAD_DETACH", "PROCESS_DETACH" }
```

The first thread started before the DLL was loaded, so it never produces a notification.
hints: Keep one integer, the reference count. Every rule is "only when the count is above zero" or "only when the count changes between zero and one".
